statement.essentials: Extracapsular dissection takes out the tumour with a thin rim of normal gland, without searching for the facial nerve.
statement.anatomy: Extracapsular dissection is classed apart from formal parotidectomy: the facial nerve is not dissected, and less than one level of the gland is removed.
statement.clinical: In the ESGS classification extracapsular dissection avoids facial nerve dissection and removes less than one level, so level I or II is recorded only to show where the tumour lay. It has been described as a minimal-margin operation.

limitations: Definitions follow the ESGS classification; individual surgeons use the term more or less strictly, and the width of the rim is not standardised (the cuff drawn here is illustrative).
